numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In iirfilter, the line Wn = 2*Wn/fs can cause an integer overflow when Wn is passed as an integer (or array of integers) stored as int32, because the multiplication by 2 is performed before the division by fs.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Wn should be normalized without integer overflow; the fix reorders the operation to Wn = Wn / (fs/2) so the multiplication by 2 no longer overflows for large integer Wn values.
trigger_conditions: Wn passed as an integer or array of integers (stored as int32)
Wn large enough that multiplying by 2 overflows int32
fs is specified (not None) and analog is False

oracle_clues: PR #20456 'BUG: signal.iirfilter: avoid integer overflow' fixes issue #20455
Fix changes line Wn = 2*Wn/fs to Wn = Wn / (fs/2) in scipy/signal/_filter_design.py
Attempting in-place Wn /= (fs/2) raises numpy _UFuncOutputCastingError (float64 to int32, same_kind rule), so the fix is not in-place
Existing assertion in test_int_inputs checks k2 = 9.999999999999989e+47 with assert_allclose

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Wn values around 1e9 (e.g. Wn=[1000000000, 1100000000]) with fs=6250000000 can overflow int32 when computing 2*Wn/fs
category_specific_evidence: The line 2*Wn/fs can cause an integer overflow when Wn is passed as (an array of) integers since it is stored as int32 (PR#20456 body)
Test added in test_int_inputs: iirfilter(20, [1000000000, 1100000000], btype='bp', analog=False, fs=6250000000) should not raise an exception (test_diff)
Fix reorders the operation to Wn / (fs/2) to avoid overflow when Wn is integer and large enough that multiplying by 2 overflows (commit message)
Attempting the in-place division fails with numpy UFuncOutputCastingError: cannot cast ufunc 'divide' output from float64 to int32 under same_kind casting (discussion)
Existing assertion in test_int_inputs checks k2 = 9.999999999999989e+47 with assert_allclose, the only stated numerical expected value
Discussion notes the normalized Wn ends up as a float either way, so integer input acceptance is not problematic
reproduction_risks: Exact overflow threshold and the integer width behavior are only described qualitatively; the reproduction must use integer Wn with fs such that 2*Wn overflows int32
In-place Wn /= (fs/2) raises a casting error for integer arrays, so the non-in-place form is needed

provenance.value: The expression 2*Wn/fs in iirfilter can cause an integer overflow when Wn is passed as an integer (or array of integers) stored as int32, because the multiplication by 2 is performed before the division by fs.
Wn should be normalized without integer overflow; the commit reorders the operation to Wn / (fs/2) so that the multiplication by 2 no longer overflows for large integer Wn values.
Wn values around 1e9 (e.g. Wn=[1000000000, 1100000000]) with fs=6250000000 can overflow int32 when computing 2*Wn/fs

In iirfilter, the line Wn = 2*Wn/fs can cause an integer overflow when Wn is passed as an integer (or array of integers) stored as int32, because the multiplication by 2 is performed before the division by fs.
Wn should be normalized without integer overflow; the fix reorders the operation to Wn = Wn / (fs/2) so the multiplication by 2 no longer overflows for large integer Wn values.
